tier_reason: The README Performance section gives first-party timings against tweetnacl-js and noble-ed25519 on an Intel i7-10700 in Chromium 93. The harness is public (test/performance.js runs test-watsign.js, test-tweetnacl-js.js and test-noble-ed25519.js through chrode, with timing in test/perf.js), but there are no engine flags or build settings, so this is C, not A.

corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark from the project's own repo. The harness is test/performance.js, which runs test/test-watsign.js, test/test-tweetnacl-js.js and test/test-noble-ed25519.js via chrode (headless Chromium), with timing in test/perf.js. The Performance section dates from October 2021 (commit 'cleaner perf test, add comparison with noble-ed25519', 2021-10-06) on Chromium 93 and has not been revalidated on modern V8 or hardware. The 'up to 33x' figure comes from a single cold-start sample (sign long msg: 43.88 ms vs 1.32 ms), and the README says cold-start runs vary between runs. The steady-state figure is 4-6x (derived from page data: 4.3x sign short, 5.1x verify short, 5.9x sign long, 5.6x verify long). Against noble-ed25519, page data gives 1.3-2.8x warm, which the README rounds to 1.2-3x. Last commit 2024-04-15 (v0.1.9), about 2.4 years before today.

notes: The claims match the README exactly and the ratios check out against the listed timings. The only real fix is the benchmark script path: the record's caveats pointed to src-experiments/test/, but the scripts live in test/. Metadata confirmed: MIT, not a fork, not archived, 14 stars, last commit 2024-04-15, so stale is correct.
